--[ Introduction

Welcome to issue 0x01. Volume 0x00, because nothing is released yet.

<b>Castaway</b> is a ten-hour lo-fi video for YouTube: one tiny island, one
tall palm, one raft, and a young woman in cream headphones with 0x8ca0
seconds to fill. She idles. She nods to the music. Every so often, on
the next bar, something happens: her bottle washes straight back, a
drone delivers more headphones, a coconut walks off worn by a hermit
crab. Then she goes back to nodding. That is the main attraction.

An unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver Johnny Castaway.
Sunny, hand-painted and always daytime, with more than 0x5a (90)
activities on four timers and every sound synthesized from code. Still
in development. The rest of this issue is paperwork.

    $ python <a href="tools/serve.py">tools/serve.py</a>        then open <a href="http://127.0.0.1:8765/">http://127.0.0.1:8765/</a>

<details>
<summary><b>0x02</b> &nbsp;Washback: letters that came straight back (questions, answered in brackets)</summary>

<pre>
                               ==<b>Castaway</b>==

                Volume 0x00, Issue 0x01, File #0x02 of 0x08

|=-----------------------------------------------------------------------=|
|=------------=[ <b>Washback: Letters That Came Straight Back</b> ]=------------=|
|=-----------------------------------------------------------------------=|
|=-----------------------------=[ the sea ]=-----------------------------=|
|=-----------------------------------------------------------------------=|

All correspondence for this desk arrives by bottle, and most of it is
ours. Letters are printed as they washed up. Replies are in square
brackets, which is how you can tell we are being serious.

|=[ 0x01 ]=--------------------------------------------------------------=|

  Hello? Is anybody out there? I am on a very small island with one
  palm.

  [ This letter washed straight back to its sender, in its own bottle.
    We are counting it as a letter to the editor. A different bottle
    brings a real reply, later in the video. Keep writing. ]

|=[ 0x02 ]=--------------------------------------------------------------=|

  Does anything actually happen?

  [ Yes. Every 2 to 5 minutes, something small. Every 12 to 25,
    something odd. A bit more than once an hour, a set piece. Every 3 to
    6 hours, something big. She is busy about a third of the time, and
    the other two thirds are the point. See file 0x03. ]

|=[ 0x03 ]=--------------------------------------------------------------=|

  When does it get dark?

  [ It does not. Always daytime is a project rule. The sun has been
    informed and has not objected. ]

|=[ 0x04 ]=--------------------------------------------------------------=|

  What is she listening to?

  [ A seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major, synthesized from
    code like every other sound here. Nobody has heard it yet. She nods
    anyway. See file 0x06. ]

|=[ 0x05 ]=--------------------------------------------------------------=|

  Where can I watch it?

  [ Nowhere yet. No video has been published and there is no link. You
    can run it yourself (file 0x07) and watch it at
    <a href="http://127.0.0.1:8765/">http://127.0.0.1:8765/</a>, which is as local as it gets. ]

|=[ 0x06 ]=--------------------------------------------------------------=|

  Is this the old screensaver?

  [ No. It is an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines
    of Johnny Castaway (1992), which belongs to its owners. New island,
    new castaway, new art, new code. Same idea, though: wait long enough
    and something happens. ]

|=[ 0x07 ]=--------------------------------------------------------------=|

  Is the cat coming back?

  [ Yes, another time. See file 0x05. Please do not ask the cat. ]

</pre>

<details>
<summary><b>0x03</b> &nbsp;Table of Tides: the schedule, in hex, with a hexdump of an hour</summary>

<pre>
---[  Castaway   Volume 0x00, Issue 0x01, Oct 2nd 2026, file 0x03 of 0x08


-------------------------[  <b>Table of Tides: The Schedule, in Hex</b>


--------[  <a href="activities.toml">activities.toml</a>, transcribed by the Tideline Desk


Everything she and her visitors can do lives in <a href="activities.toml">activities.toml</a>: more
than 0x5a (90) activities, 0x5e (94) at the count on 2026-10-02, and
more arrive every few hours. Each tier keeps its own timer. When one
goes off, an activity from that tier is picked by weight, from those
free to go. If two tiers are due at once, the rarer one wins.

  tier        every (seconds)   that is       per 10 h
  ----------  ----------------  ------------  -------------
  regular     0x78 to 0x12c     2 to 5 min    ~0x9b  (155)
  occasional  0x2d0 to 0x5dc    12 to 25 min  ~0x1e  (30)
  rare        0x708 to 0xe10    30 to 60 min  ~0x0d  (13)
  super rare  0x2a30 to 0x5460  3 to 6 hours  ~0x02  (2)
  chained     never on a timer: started by another activity ending

  Per-10-hour counts are the median of 0xc8 (200) simulated runs, plus
  about 0x14 chained follow-ups. Super rare: 0x03 at most per run.
  Decimal in brackets, for readers who are not on an island.

--[ Footnotes, in the sand

  - Every activity starts on the next bar of the music: every 0x03
    seconds. The gags land on the beat.
  - Lanes let things overlap. She has one lane; the cat, the turtle, the
    sea and sky, the shore and the kumara patch each have their own. So
    a ship can cross while she is busy with a coconut. The ship waits
    for her to get busy first. It has manners.
  - She is busy about a third of the time. In hex that is 0x0.5555...,
    which repeats forever, much like the theme.
  - Default run: 0x8ca0 seconds (10:00:00), seed 0x7c8 (1992). Check it
    and simulate one: python <a href="tools/schedule.py">tools/schedule.py</a>

--[ A hexdump of an hour

One byte per minute; each byte is what started in that minute.
Illustrative: the regular, occasional and rare timers rolled with a
seeded coin, not a real run of the scheduler.

0000  2e 72 2e 72 2e 2e 72 2e  6f 2e 2e 52 2e 2e 72 2e  |.r.r..r.o..R..r.|
0010  2e 2e 72 2e 2e 72 2e 2e  2e 2e 72 2e 2e 2e 6f 2e  |..r..r....r...o.|
0020  2e 2e 72 2e 2e 2e 2e 72  2e 2e 2e 72 2e 2e 72 2e  |..r....r...r..r.|
0030  2e 72 52 2e 72 2e 6f 2e  72 2e 2e 72              |.rR.r.o.r..r|

  2e "." nothing new   72 "r" regular   6f "o" occasional   52 "R" rare
</pre>

<summary><b>0x04</b> &nbsp;Tidewrack: things that washed up (the gags)</summary>

<pre>
                               ==<b>Castaway</b>==

                Volume 0x00, Issue 0x01, File #0x04 of 0x08

XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX

                     <b>Tidewrack: Things That Washed Up</b>

             compiled by the tide, which takes most of it back

XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX

Things that turn up on the island, in the order the desk found them.
Every one of them starts on the beat. None of them are rescue.

[0x01] <b>BOTTLE RETURNED TO SENDER</b>
       She throws a message in a bottle. It washes straight back. Much
       later, a different bottle brings a reply. Correspondence is open.

[0x02] <b>PARCEL DELIVERED BY AIR</b>
       A delivery drone lowers a parcel. Inside: another pair of
       headphones.

[0x03] <b>TURTLE, VISITING</b>
       A sea turtle swims in and crawls up beside her, and they both
       doze off. Meeting adjourned.

[0x04] <b>CAT, ARRIVING BY CRATE</b>
       A grey tabby with a white chest. Climbs the palm. Naps. See file
       0x05.

[0x05] <b>SIGNAL LOCATED</b>
       One bar, at the very top of the palm. She has to climb for it.
       This issue was sent from there.

[0x06] <b>SHARK, IN HEADPHONES</b>
       A shark surfaces wearing headphones and nods to the beat.

[0x07] <b>TOURISM</b>
       A small tour boat pulls up and everyone takes a selfie. She is in
       the background of all of them. Nobody offers a lift.

[0x08] <b>COCONUT LEAVES ISLAND ON FOOT</b>
       A coconut falls on a hermit crab. Then the coconut walks off,
       with the crab wearing it.

[0x09] <b>SHE COULD LEAVE ANY TIME</b>
       She walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee.
       Nobody asks.

[0x0a] <b>HYDROFOIL</b>
       A bro on an electric hydrofoil waves a shaka and carves off.

[0x0b] <b>BUSHCRAFT</b>
       Fire by friction. A hammock. A lookout up the palm. Spear
       fishing.

[0x0c] <b>AGRICULTURE</b>
       She plants a kumara. It grows over the course of the video.

[0x0d] <b>RESCUE, ALMOST</b>
       She finally spots a ship and waves like mad. It sounds its horn
       back. Then it sails on. She puts the music back on.

[0x0e] <b>EVERYDAY</b>
       Coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, and a sandcastle that the
       tide takes.

--[ In the offing

Visible from the shore, or coming soon, which is what the phrase means
either way. Scene life: 26 entries, 4 always-on effects and 22 timed
events. Built so far: shore waves and drifting cloud shadows. Planned:
distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins,
sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower (in daylight).
</pre>

Castaway, File #0x06 of 0x08
Volume 0x00, Issue 0x01, Released: October 2, 2026


                 <b>Signal and Noise: Every Sound, From Code</b>
                 ----------------------------------------
                    by <a href="tools/make_audio.py">tools/make_audio.py</a>, with notes


Every sound in Castaway is synthesized from code, in
<a href="tools/make_audio.py">tools/make_audio.py</a>. No samples, no loops, no recordings, so no
third-party licence applies. More than 0x96 (150) sound files so far,
all made the same way.

  the theme .... a seamless 0x3c-second loop (60)
  tempo ........ 0x50 BPM (80)
  key .......... F major
  changes ...... Gm9 | C13 | Fmaj9 | Dm9 (ii-V-I-vi, a chord a bar)
  bars ......... 0x14 (20), exactly 0x03 seconds each: round 0x05 times
  the band ..... electric piano, kalimba lead, soft drums, vinyl crackle
  the ocean .... also a seamless 0x3c-second loop
  loudness ..... -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP
  in hex ....... no. negative numbers stay in decimal, out of respect
  the knobs .... a master level, and one per routine

--[ Errata

Nobody has listened to any of it yet. It is code; it may be lovely. A
full review follows in issue 0x02, once somebody presses play.
</pre>

|=-------------------=[ tools/serve.py and friends ]=--------------------=|
|=-----------------------------------------------------------------------=|

--[ Making landfall

  $ python <a href="tools/serve.py">tools/serve.py</a>
      The renderer. Open <a href="http://127.0.0.1:8765/">http://127.0.0.1:8765/</a> for a live preview, then
      export: frames are encoded in the browser (WebCodecs H.264, 68 to
      78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), and the server mixes the
      sound and joins the two into a YouTube-ready MP4.

  $ python <a href="tools/schedule.py">tools/schedule.py</a>
      Validates the schedule and simulates a 10-hour run.

  $ python <a href="tools/render_demo.py">tools/render_demo.py</a> --dev
      A dev reel of every activity, with a heads-up display (the older
      Python reference renderer).

--[ What you will not need

  - a build step
  - npm packages (plain ES modules only)
  - a boat

--[ House style

  picture ....... 16:9, 1080p, 0x1e (30) frames a second
  motion ........ hard cuts and stepped movement, by default
  lighting ...... always daytime. there are no night scenes
  the page ...... <a href="web/index.html">web/index.html</a>
  the logbook ... <a href="MUSING.md">MUSING.md</a>, where the decisions are written down

--[ Greets

Waves across the water to the sea turtle, the grey tabby (wherever it is
today), the hermit crab and its coconut, the shark with the good
headphones, the bro on the hydrofoil (shaka returned), the selfie boat,
the drone, the kumara, and the tide, for taking the sandcastle so
politely.

And to Johnny Castaway, the 1992 screensaver that started all this: an
unofficial nod, with respect. It belongs to its owners. This island, its
art, its code and every sound on it are new. The Tideline Desk is made
up. The waiting is real.
